name: Leah Silber

bio.statement: The City of Rivergrove city council page lists Leah Silber as a councilor.

source.publisher: City of Rivergrove, City Council page

bio.statement: Her campaign site says she was appointed to the Rivergrove City Council in March 2024 to fill a vacated seat.
bio.excerpt: I was appointed to the Rivergrove City Council in March 2024 to fill a vacated seat.

bio.statement: Silber's pamphlet statement lists her as a local software company CEO with management experience at Silicon Valley software companies.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Local Software Company CEO Occupational Background: Management at Silicon Valley software companies, focused on Operations, Marketing and HR.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 48, printed C-47)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists Rivergrove City Councilor since 2024, VP of the League of Oregon Cities Women's Caucus, and ODOT's Small Cities Allotment Advisory Committee.
bio.excerpt: Rivergrove City Councilor since 2024. VP, League of Oregon Cities Women’s Caucus. Served on regional committees, including ODOT’s Small Cities Allotment Advisory Committee.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 48, printed C-47)

positions.statement: Silber says she was the only councilor who voted against proposing a new Rivergrove tax, which she says Rivergrove rejected in May.
positions.excerpt: I’m the only councilor who voted against pitching a new Rivergrove tax, and in May, Rivergrove rejected it decisively.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 48, printed C-47)

positions.statement: Silber says the city should spend on what residents need, get competitive bids before hiring, follow budget law and act on the recent audit's findings.
positions.excerpt: We should spend on what residents need, get competitive bids before hiring, start following budget law, and act on everything the recent audit found.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 48, printed C-47)

positions.statement: Silber says the city needs safe and easy river access for all and to get its sewer, flood and other infrastructure in order.
positions.excerpt: We need safe and easy river access for all, and to get our sewer, flood and other infrastructure in order.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026 (PDF p. 48, printed C-47)

positions.statement: Silber's campaign site says residents have a right to know how their tax dollars are managed.
positions.excerpt: Residents have a right to know how their tax dollars are being managed.

gaps: No endorsements listed in her pamphlet statement (she names Joan Joyce and David Dull as running mates)
No sourced position on housing or public safety
